mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth by more than 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of quarters with negative GDP growth, or the correlation between GDP growth and SPX returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production by more than 2% month-over-month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the same month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased consumer confidence and spending.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decrease > 0.3% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE decrease and PAYEMS increase on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month, coupled with a decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5%, signals a positive demand environment with controlled inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 10% and CPIAUCSL decrease > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the joint effect of HOUST increase and CPIAUCSL decrease on SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as liquidity increases and borrowing costs decrease.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real retail and food services sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and SPX returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
